item.description:
STORY | Should have won Nobel Prize eight times for each war I settled: Trump

US President Donald Trump slammed Norway for passing him over for the Nobel Peace Prize, claiming he should have won it eight times for each war he settled.

Addressing a rally in Syracuse on Friday, Trump also claimed to have saved 50 million lives by preventing nuclear armed India and Pakistan from going to war.

“The United States of America, represented by me as your president, should have received the Nobel Peace Prize, but didn’t. And this is an indelible stain on the country of Norway, and those people that made such a disgraceful and embarrassing decision,” Trump said.

“The Nobel Peace Prize has been forever discredited by a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation. We will not forget, Norway, that you didn’t give this prize,” the US President said.

The Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief, whom Trump says is someone “nobody ever heard of”.

item.title: VIDEO | Singapore: Indian driver Kush Maini will extend his association with the Alpine Formula 1 team to 2027 after failing to secure a race seat fol...
item.description:
VIDEO | Singapore: Indian driver Kush Maini will extend his association with the Alpine Formula 1 team to 2027 after failing to secure a race seat following four rollercoaster seasons in Formula 2.

In his fourth and final Formula 2 season, Maini is ninth in the standings with 90 points. With Alpine retaining Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto for the next Formula 1 season, Maini will once again have to remain on the sidelines.

It is not yet clear in what capacity Maini will remain part of the Enstone-based team. He joined the Alpine Academy in 2023 before becoming a reserve driver for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.

“All the four tests (with Alpine) have gone really well, like they always have. I feel like I'm a part of the family. It has been three years now, and I do a lot of simulator work for them. I'm pretty sure our relationship will continue.

“I feel a part of the team, and they really like having me around and being on the simulator. So I'll definitely be with Alpine in the future. Now, it's still not decided what role it would be, but overall, that's where we are right now,” said Maini.

item.description:
🇳🇵 🚨 NEPAL: THREAT ACTOR CLAIMS TO SELL MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS DIPLOMATIC DATA

A threat actor on an underground forum is advertising what they claim is data stolen from Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA).

The listing claims the data includes:
* Records of talks with foreign embassies, naming India, Pakistan and Bangladesh "and many more"
* Diplomatic talks
* Bilateral meeting records
* Material on a Nepali Air Defence trainee program

The seller says samples are shared only in private chat and asks for "serious buyers" only. No sample was reviewed, and no file size, record count or price is given in the post.

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The post is short on detail and offers no public proof, so this could be overstated or recycled. If genuine, internal diplomatic records involving Nepal's neighbours would be valuable for espionage, targeted phishing of diplomats and political pressure, which matters more here than the volume of data. It follows several recent claims against Nepali government systems.

This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs was breached.

item.description:
⚠️ GHOSTACTION RETURNS: FAKE "SECURITY AUDIT" GITHUB WORKFLOWS ARE STEALING CI/CD AND CLOUD SECRETS

Socket says more than 500 GitHub accounts have committed a credential-stealing GitHub Actions workflow to tens of thousands of repositories since Oct 7, using what appear to be stolen maintainer credentials.

• Workflow named security-audit.yml (or github_actions_security.yml), committed under the victim's own identity
• Steals the repo's Actions secrets AND sweeps the full git history for AWS, OpenAI, Anthropic, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Google and SendGrid keys
• Oct 8 burst hit 346 repos via the henrywoo and kitao accounts, including uber/athenadriver and kitao/pyxel
• Data is POSTed to 193.32.204[.]199

No malicious PyPI or http://crates.io releases observed so far. If you find the file: remove it, rotate every secret it names, scan full history (not just HEAD) and treat the account as compromised.

Primary:
socket[.]dev/blog/ghostaction-cloud-credentials

🇯🇵🇩🇪 🚨 SUSPECTED QILIN RANSOMWARE CORE MEMBER ARRESTED IN JAPAN, EXTRADITED TO GERMANY

Japan's National Police Agency (NPA) confirmed on Oct 8, 2026 that Japanese police helped Germany arrest a Russian national believed to be a leading member of the Qilin ransomware group.

What officials say:
• Germany held an arrest warrant over a ransomware attack on a German company
• Japanese police detained the suspect after he travelled to Japan, under Japan's extradition law
• He was handed over to Germany with Japan's Justice Ministry and the Tokyo High Public Prosecutors Office
• NRW Interior Minister Herbert Reul called it a "historic" success for the state's LKA and ZAC cybercrime units
• Reul said Qilin has hit nearly 4,000 organisations worldwide, about 150 in Germany

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The suspect's name has not been officially released, and reported details (age 28, arrested in Osaka in May) come from media accounts. Qilin runs as ransomware-as-a-service, so one arrest is unlikely to stop its affiliates; the group listed new victims as recently as this month.

item.title: 🚨 $86M+ IN SUSPECTED LEDGER WALLET DRAINS — COMPANY INVESTIGATES RESELLER Ledger has confirmed an investigation into reports of cryptocurrency dis...
item.description:
🚨 $86M+ IN SUSPECTED LEDGER WALLET DRAINS — COMPANY INVESTIGATES RESELLER

Ledger has confirmed an investigation into reports of cryptocurrency disappearing from customers’ hardware wallets.

On-chain investigator Specter estimates more than $86 MILLION in suspected losses across Bitcoin, Ethereum and TRON.

Some affected users claim their recovery phrases were stored offline and their wallets had minimal interaction with decentralized applications.

The investigation has now taken a significant turn.

Ledger says the reported losses involve customers in Southeast Asia who purchased devices from a reseller named CryptoBilis.

As a precaution:

Ledger has asked CryptoBilis to suspend device sales and shipments
Customers who purchased devices from the reseller within the past 90 days are advised not to initialize them
Customers who already initialized affected devices are advised to consider transferring assets to a new Ledger signer with a newly generated recovery phrase
Investigators are examining whether the incidents involve compromised devices or distribution channels

⚠️ IMPORTANT:

The $86M+ figure is an independent on-chain estimate, NOT a loss amount confirmed by Ledger.

There is currently no confirmed evidence of a universal Ledger hardware or firmware vulnerability.

A potential supply-chain compromise has been suggested, but the attack mechanism remains under investigation.

⚠️ Analyst Note:

Hardware wallets are designed to keep private keys isolated.

But their security also depends on device authenticity, secure initialization and the integrity of the supply chain.

If attackers can compromise devices before customers receive them, offline recovery-phrase storage alone may not prevent theft.

This investigation could have significant implications for hardware-wallet distribution and trust.

#DDW #Ledger #CryptoSecurity #CyberCrime #SupplyChainSecurity

item.title: ⭐️🚨 TELEGRAM STARS EXPLOIT ALLEGEDLY GENERATED $4.5M — GIFT TRANSACTIONS UNDER SCRUTINY Telegram’s collectible-gift ecosystem is facing reports...
item.description:
⭐️🚨 TELEGRAM STARS EXPLOIT ALLEGEDLY GENERATED $4.5M — GIFT TRANSACTIONS UNDER SCRUTINY

Telegram’s collectible-gift ecosystem is facing reports of a potentially serious refund and accounting vulnerability.

According to Telegram-community reports, an individual allegedly exploited the platform over approximately two months, generating $4.5 million worth of Stars and withdrawing around $1.5 million.

The alleged scheme involved:

Selling collectible gifts through Telegram’s marketplace
Moving Stars between accounts and bots
Refunding earlier transactions
Creating inconsistent balances while retaining transferred value
Repeating the process to accumulate additional Stars

Several high-value collectibles, including MirageLamp and LuckyLocket items, have reportedly become unavailable or subject to transfer restrictions.

⚠️ IMPORTANT:

The $4.5M figure, $1.5M withdrawal claim and full exploit mechanism remain independently unverified.

Telegram has not publicly confirmed those amounts or provided a technical incident report.

⚠️ Analyst Note:

If confirmed, this would represent a potentially serious transaction-integrity failure rather than a conventional wallet compromise.

The central issue is whether refunds can reverse a transaction without consistently reversing the value transferred to other accounts.

In digital asset marketplaces, maintaining consistency between payments, ownership, refunds and withdrawals is critical.

For now, collectible-gift traders should exercise caution with assets potentially affected by disputed transactions.

https://t.me/s/crypto_gst

Medical device company iRhythm Technologies has begun mailing breach notices to patients and filing them with state regulators, including the California Attorney General.

item.title: 🇸🇦 🚨 SAUDI ARABIA: TAMIMI GROUP — 310 GB OF CORPORATE DATA WITH 522K+ ID/PASSPORT MATCHES ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE A threat actor on an undergroun...
item.description:
🇸🇦 🚨 SAUDI ARABIA: TAMIMI GROUP — 310 GB OF CORPORATE DATA WITH 522K+ ID/PASSPORT MATCHES ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE

A threat actor on an underground forum claims to be selling 310 GB of data (more than 320,000 files) allegedly belonging to Tamimi Group (tamimigroup[.]com[.]sa), a Saudi Arabian conglomerate, describing it as covering "all company activities".

The listing claims:
* 522,662 passport, residence permit and national ID matches
* 78,365 phone numbers
* 47,248 email addresses
* 22,763 credential-like entries
* 188 IBANs that pass checksum validation

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The counts read like the output of an automated scan across the stolen files rather than a count of unique people, so duplicates are likely and the number of affected individuals may be far lower. If genuine, ID and passport data, bank account numbers and credentials from a large employer create risk of identity fraud, invoice or payroll fraud, and follow-on intrusion. The actor offers samples privately; they were not reviewed.

This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Tamimi Group was breached.

item.title: 🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: FICTION EXPRESS EDUCATION PLATFORM — 725 GB OF STUDENT, TEACHER AND SCHOOL DATA ALLEGEDLY STOLEN A threat actor on an undergroun...
item.description:
🇪🇸 🚨 SPAIN: FICTION EXPRESS EDUCATION PLATFORM — 725 GB OF STUDENT, TEACHER AND SCHOOL DATA ALLEGEDLY STOLEN

A threat actor on an underground forum claims to have stolen 725 GB of data allegedly belonging to Fiction Express (fictionexpress[.]com), a Spanish digital reading platform used by schools, and is demanding a $100,000 ransom before selling it.

The listing claims:
* 2,928,795 student records, including 101,084 individually named minors
* 121,092 teacher records
* 37,670 school records (owner names, emails, phone numbers, addresses)
* 1,297,119 student voice recordings (MP3)
* Names, emails, usernames, school and classroom details

The claim has not been independently verified.

⚠️ Analyst Note:
The listing shows field names only and no sample records, so the size and authenticity of the dataset cannot be confirmed. If genuine, it would expose children's data and voice recordings. Schools, teachers and parents should expect phishing that impersonates the platform or their school. The actor says the data will be sold if the ransom is not paid.

This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Fiction Express was breached.

PTI INFOGRAPHICS | UPDATE: 45 Delhi Metro stations to stay shut ahead of Oct 10 protest

Entry and exit gates at 45 Delhi Metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, New Delhi, Central Secretariat and Kashmere Gate, will remain closed from 9 pm on Friday till 6 pm on Saturday due to security reasons ahead of a proposed protest at Jantar Mantar.

In a revised update, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) cut the list from the 57 stations announced earlier and said the situation will be reviewed by security agencies, while the interchange facility will remain available at all the concerned stations except New Delhi.
